mainTopic: Learning from "את", and the ban on benefit from עגלה ערופה and ציפורי מצורע: its source and when it begins
overview: The גמרא first explains that one opinion does not learn laws from the little word "את". It backs this up with the story of שמעון העמסוני, who stopped expounding "את" at "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא", until רבי עקיבא taught that this "את" includes תלמידי חכמים. Next, the גמרא returns to the משנה's list. It learns that an עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit from the word כפרה, just like קדשים. It learns that ציפורי מצורע are forbidden because the item that enables is treated like the item that atones. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש then argue about when the birds become forbidden: at שחיטה, or already when they are taken. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש three times. The last challenge pushes ריש לקיש to say the issue is an argument among תנאים. Finally, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא gives the permitting פסוק to the sent-away bird and not to the slaughtered one. רב שמואל בר רב יצחק begins to challenge the answer, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: This opinion does not learn from the word "את"
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion did not use the word "את" as its source because he does not learn laws from "את" at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not expound the word "את".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the other opinion did not learn the law from the word "את": he simply never learns laws from that word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some חכמים treat "את" as an extra word that adds something to the law. This opinion treats it as a normal part of the sentence with nothing extra to teach. So for him the law has to come from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: A small Hebrew word that marks the object of a verb. Some חכמים learn extra laws from it.
He does not expound it, meaning he does not learn a law from it.

steps.confusionAlert: "את" here is not the word meaning "you". It is the little object-marker word that comes before a noun, like "את השמים".

phrases.english: He does not expound the word "et."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous part of the דף about why the other opinion did not use the "את" source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Method of reading: this opinion does not treat "את" as a source for laws.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since "את" appears in the פסוק, everyone should learn the law from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not everyone learns from "את". This opinion treats it as an ordinary word.

steps.title: שמעון העמסוני stopped learning from "את"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that שמעון העמסוני learned from every "את" in the תורה, until he reached "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא" and stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: שמעון העמסוני, and some say נחמיה העמסוני, used to expound every "את" in the תורה. When he reached "You shall fear את ה׳ your God," he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that there really is a view that does not learn from "את".
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון העמסוני learned an extra law from every "את". At the פסוק about fearing ה׳ he could not think of anything that could be included together with fear of ה׳. So he gave up the whole method, and that shows the approach of not learning from "את" is a real one.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא.
The many times the word "את" appears.
He separated himself, meaning he stopped using this method.
And some say, introducing a second version of a name or teaching.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Shimon HaAmasoni,
and some say it was Nechemya HaAmasoni,
would expound every "et" in the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְ״אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא״, פֵּירַשׁ.
phrases.english: Once he reached "You shall fear et ה׳ your God," he withdrew.
phrases.notes: דברים 6:13. Nothing can be feared together with ה׳, so he didn't know what this "את" could add.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by showing there was a תנא who stopped learning from "את".
steps.raayaObject: The claim that some opinions do not learn laws from "את".
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about שמעון העמסוני giving up the method at "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא".

steps.title: The students ask about all his earlier teachings
steps.stepSummary: His students ask what becomes of all the laws he already learned from "את".
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, what will happen with all the "את"s you already expounded?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, the students ask a natural question that sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the method failed in one place, then maybe all his earlier teachings from "את" are no good. The students want to know whether all that learning was wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: His students.
What will be with them, meaning what happens to them now.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Our teacher,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶתִּין שֶׁדָּרַשְׁתָּ מָה תְּהֵא עֲלֵיהֶם?
phrases.english: all the "et"s that you expounded, what will be with them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from his withdrawal in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of all the laws he previously learned from "את"?

steps.title: Reward for expounding and reward for stopping
steps.stepSummary: He answers that just as he got reward for expounding, he gets reward for stepping back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Just as I received reward for the expounding, so I received reward for the withdrawing.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון העמסוני answers his students. Both his learning and his decision to stop were a מצוה that earns reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not defend his old teachings. He says honestly stepping back from a method that does not hold up is itself worthy of reward. This confirms that in the end he no longer learned laws from "את".

keyTerms.meaning: Reward.
Expounding, learning laws from the words of a פסוק.
Withdrawing, stepping back from something.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that sincerely stepping back from a method that does not hold up is also part of learning תורה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Just as I received reward for the expounding,
so I received reward for the withdrawing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁקִּבַּלְתִּי שָׂכָר עַל הַדְּרִישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both the expounding and the withdrawal earned reward. He does not go back to the method.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the "את" includes תלמידי חכמים
steps.stepSummary: Later, רבי עקיבא explained that the "את" in "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא" comes to include fear of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until רבי עקיבא came and taught: "You shall fear את ה׳ your God" comes to include תלמידי חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by telling us that רבי עקיבא found a meaning for the "את" that שמעון העמסוני couldn't explain. We must also fear תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא kept the method of learning from "את" and solved the hard case. The fear of ה׳ extends to those who carry His תורה. Still, our point stands: שמעון העמסוני himself stopped learning from "את".

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to add something to the law.
Torah scholars.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. Some, like שמעון העמסוני after he stopped, do not learn from "את". Others, like רבי עקיבא, do learn from it, even in "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא", which includes fear of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא's teaching does not take back the proof. The ברייתא was brought only to show that some opinion does not learn from "את", and שמעון העמסוני is that opinion.

phrases.english: Until Rabbi Akiva came and taught:
"You shall fear et ה׳ your God"
comes to include Torah scholars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by giving the explanation of the "את" that stopped שמעון העמסוני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The "את" in "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא" includes fear of תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: Where do we learn the ban on benefit from עגלה ערופה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list and asks for the source that עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה listed עגלה ערופה. From where do we know it is forbidden for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list of forbidden things and asks for its source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that קידושין with an עגלה ערופה do not work because it is forbidden for benefit. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק or reasoning teaches that ban.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown.
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: With a heifer whose neck is broken: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the "את" discussion and moves on to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: "כפרה" is written by it, like קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי says the תורה uses the word כפרה by עגלה ערופה, just like by קדשים, so it is forbidden for benefit like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: The word "atonement" is written about it, just like קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. Since the עגלה ערופה brings כפרה like a קרבן, it is forbidden for benefit like a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know קדשים are forbidden for benefit. The shared word כפרה links עגלה ערופה to קדשים, so it gets the same ban.

keyTerms.meaning: The school, or students, of רבי ינאי.
Atonement.
Holy offerings, which are forbidden for personal benefit.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
"Atonement" is written about it, as with sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word כפרה is written about עגלה ערופה as it is about קדשים, so it shares their ban on benefit.

steps.title: Where do we learn the ban on benefit from ציפורי מצורע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the birds of a מצורע are forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה listed ציפורי מצורע. From where do we know they are forbidden for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list and asks for its source. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that קידושין with a מצורע's birds do not work. The גמרא looks for the source showing these birds are forbidden for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: The birds brought by a מצורע as part of his purification.

phrases.english: "The leper's birds": from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from עגלה ערופה to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a מצורע's birds are forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: Inside and outside: things that permit and things that atone
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל begins a comparison. The תורה speaks of things that permit (מכשיר) and things that atone (מכפר) inside the בית המקדש, and also of such things outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The תורה mentions something that permits and something that atones inside, and it mentions something that permits and something that atones outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. It sets up two parallel pairs, one inside the מקדש and one outside, and the comparison continues afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the מקדש, both kinds of קרבנות are forbidden for benefit, the kind that permits the person and the kind that atones. The parallel builds a pair outside the מקדש too. If the outside thing that atones is forbidden for benefit, then the outside thing that permits should be forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
Something that makes a person fit or permitted, like allowing him back in.
Something that brings atonement.
Inside the מקדש / outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Something that enables and something that atones is stated inside,
and something that enables and something that atones is stated outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is built on a comparison. There are things that permit and things that atone both inside and outside the מקדש, and the comparison is completed in the continuation.

steps.title: Finishing the comparison: what is outside follows the pattern of what is inside
steps.stepSummary: Inside the מקדש, the item that permits is treated like the item that atones. So outside the מקדש too, the permitting birds of a מצורע are treated like the atoning עגלה ערופה, and they are forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as with the permitting and atoning things said about the inside, the תורה made the permitting thing like the atoning thing, so too with the permitting and atoning things said about the outside, the תורה made the permitting thing like the atoning thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ישמעאל completes the comparison begun in step 9. Their conclusion is that the birds of a מצורע are forbidden for benefit, just like עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the מקדש, a permitting offering (the מצורע's אשם) has the same status as atoning קדשים. The school of רבי ישמעאל applies the same pattern outside the מקדש. The permitting birds take on the status of the atoning עגלה ערופה, which is already known to be forbidden for benefit (step 7).

keyTerms.meaning: Something that permits or 'makes fit', like the birds that allow a מצורע to become pure
Something that atones
Inside the בית המקדש
Outside the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The birds of a מצורע are forbidden for benefit because the תורה treats them like עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: Just as with the permitting and atoning things stated inside
phrases.notes: Inside, the 'permitting' thing is the מצורע's אשם offering, and the 'atoning' thing is קדשים in general.

phrases.english: it made the permitting thing like the atoning thing,
so too the permitting and atoning things stated outside:
phrases.notes: Outside, the 'permitting' thing is the מצורע's birds, and the 'atoning' thing is עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: it made the permitting thing like the atoning thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison that began in step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The birds of a מצורע are forbidden for benefit, just like עגלה ערופה, because the item that permits is treated like the item that atones.

steps.title: Dispute: from when are the birds of a מצורע forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the birds become forbidden from שחיטה. ריש לקיש says they become forbidden from the moment they are taken for the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: From when are the birds of a מצורע forbidden? רבי יוחנן said: from the time of שחיטה. ריש לקיש said: from the time of taking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows that the birds are forbidden, so it brings a dispute about when that ban starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about timing, not about whether the birds are forbidden at all. רבי יוחנן ties the ban to שחיטה. ריש לקיש starts it earlier, when the birds are taken and set aside for the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated' (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
From the time of slaughter
From the time of taking, when the birds are chosen for the מצורע

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that the birds are forbidden. They only argue about when the ban begins.

phrases.english: It was stated: from when are the birds of a מצורע forbidden?
רבי יוחנן said: from the time of slaughter,
and ריש לקיש said: from the time of taking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ban proven in step 10 and asks when it starts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the ban starts at שחיטה. ריש לקיש: the ban starts when the birds are taken.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוחנן, the שחיטה itself is what forbids the birds. ריש לקיש learns from עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden while still alive, so the birds are also forbidden while alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said from the time of שחיטה, because it is the שחיטה that forbids it. ריש לקיש said from the time of taking, because he learns it from עגלה ערופה: just as עגלה ערופה is forbidden while alive, so too the birds of a מצורע are forbidden while alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of each side in the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן sees שחיטה as the act that creates the ban. ריש לקיש notes that the birds' ban is learned from עגלה ערופה (step 10). Since עגלה ערופה is forbidden while still alive, the birds should be too, even before they are slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It comes out', meaning it is learned from
While alive

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said from the time of slaughter,
because it is the slaughter that forbids it.
ריש לקיש said from the time of taking,
because it is learned from עגלה ערופה:
just as עגלה ערופה is forbidden while alive,
so too the birds of a מצורע are forbidden while alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מִשְּׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה, שְׁחִיטָה הוּא דְּאָסְרָה לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of both opinions in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש compares the birds to עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden while alive. רבי יוחנן holds that only שחיטה creates the ban.

steps.title: From when is עגלה ערופה itself forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks at what point עגלה ערופה itself becomes forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עגלה ערופה itself, from when is it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש's view depends on עגלה ערופה, so the גמרא asks exactly when עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden. This sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ריש לקיש's whole view is built on comparing the birds to עגלה ערופה, we need to know the exact timing for עגלה ערופה. The answer could either help ריש לקיש or work against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From when

phrases.english: And עגלה ערופה itself, from when is it forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks into the source case that ריש לקיש relies on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact moment when עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden for benefit

steps.title: רבי ינאי forgot; the scholars say going down to the valley forbids it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says he once heard the point at which עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden but forgot it. The scholars say it is its going down to the hard valley that makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: I heard a boundary about it, but I forgot. The scholars tended to say: its going down to the hard valley is what forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden when it is brought down to the valley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer means עגלה ערופה is not forbidden right when it is taken. It becomes forbidden later, when it goes down to the valley. It is still alive at that point, but this is a separate stage after the taking.

keyTerms.meaning: A boundary, here meaning the stage at which it becomes forbidden
The group of scholars
A hard, rough valley where the עגלה ערופה is brought

phrases.english: רבי ינאי said:
I heard a boundary about it, but I forgot it,
and the scholars tended to say:
its going down to the hard valley
is what forbids it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: גְּבוּל שָׁמַעְתִּי בָּהּ וְשָׁכַחְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden when it goes down to the valley.

steps.title: Challenge to ריש לקיש: then the birds should not be forbidden from the taking
steps.stepSummary: If עגלה ערופה is not forbidden from the moment it is taken, then the birds learned from it should not be forbidden from the taking either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as עגלה ערופה is not forbidden from the time of taking, so too the birds of a מצורע should not be forbidden from the time of taking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer of step 14 to challenge ריש לקיש's own comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the birds follow עגלה ערופה. But עגלה ערופה only becomes forbidden at the valley, not at the taking. So the comparison seems to show that the birds should not be forbidden at the taking either.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not forbidden

phrases.english: If so, just as עגלה ערופה
is not forbidden from the time of taking,
so too the birds of a מצורע also
should not be forbidden from the time of taking!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה מִשְּׁעַת לְקִיחָה לָא מִיתַּסְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 14 against ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the birds are forbidden from the time of taking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His source, עגלה ערופה, is not forbidden at the taking, so the case learned from it should not be either.

steps.title: Defense: the birds have no other boundary
steps.stepSummary: The cases are different. עגלה ערופה has another stage, going down to the valley, that can forbid it. The birds have no other stage before שחיטה, so the taking must be what forbids them.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, it has another boundary. Here, does it have another boundary?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge and defends ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עגלה ערופה can wait for the valley stage because that stage exists. The birds have no such middle stage. So for them, being forbidden 'while alive' can only begin at the taking.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so now?!', meaning the comparison doesn't work
Another

phrases.english: How can you compare them?!
There, it has another boundary,
phrases.notes: Meaning the going down to the valley from step 14.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא מִי אִית לֵיהּ גְּבוּל אַחֲרִינָא?!
phrases.english: here, does it have another boundary?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two cases are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The birds should match עגלה ערופה exactly in timing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The birds have no middle stage, so being forbidden while alive must begin at the taking.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from the פסוק that forbids the slaughtered bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses a פסוק to forbid the slaughtered bird. If the bird were already forbidden while alive, why would we need a פסוק to forbid it after שחיטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: 'Every pure bird you may eat' comes to include the bird that is sent away. 'And these are the ones you shall not eat of them' comes to include the slaughtered one. If you think it is forbidden while alive, is a פסוק needed to forbid it after שחיטה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא to challenge ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needs a פסוק to forbid the slaughtered bird. That suggests the bird was not forbidden before. If ריש לקיש were right, the ban would already be in place while it was alive, and the פסוק would seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a ברייתא
The bird that is sent away
The slaughtered bird
Is it needed?

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש:
'Every pure bird you may eat'
comes to include the one that is sent away,
phrases.notes: The מצורע brings two birds. One is slaughtered and the other is set free, and that one is permitted.

phrases.english: 'And these are the ones you shall not eat of them'
comes to include the slaughtered one.
And if you think it is forbidden while alive,
is a פסוק needed to forbid it after slaughter?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the birds are forbidden while alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that forbids the bird after שחיטה would be unneeded if it were already forbidden while alive.

steps.title: Answer: the פסוק teaches that שחיטה does not permit it, unlike קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed. Without it, we might think the birds are like קדשים, which are forbidden while alive but become permitted to eat once slaughtered. The פסוק teaches that the slaughtered bird stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said it is like קדשים, which are forbidden while alive, and then שחיטה comes and makes them permitted. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי יוחנן's challenge and defends ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not create the ban. It keeps the ban from ending at שחיטה. Without the פסוק, we might have compared the birds to קדשים, where שחיטה makes the meat permitted to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said', meaning what we would have thought otherwise
Just as it is with
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש survives this challenge: the פסוק is needed to teach that שחיטה does not permit the bird, unlike קדשים.

phrases.english: You might have said
it is just like קדשים,
which are forbidden while alive,
and then slaughter comes and makes them permitted,
so the פסוק teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the פסוק a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שחיטה might make the bird permitted, as it does for קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that the slaughtered bird stays forbidden even after שחיטה.

steps.title: A slaughtered bird found to be a טריפה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה. If a slaughtered bird turns out to be a טריפה, another bird is taken in its place, and the first bird is permitted for benefit. If the bird were forbidden while still alive, why would it be permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If he slaughtered the bird and it turned out to be a טריפה, he takes a new partner for the second bird, and the first bird is permitted for benefit. If you think the bird is forbidden while alive, why is the first one permitted for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a משנה to show that ריש לקיש's view does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the bird became forbidden once it was taken for the מצוה, while it was still alive. Finding out later that it is a טריפה should not remove a prohibition that already took effect. The משנה permits it anyway, which fits רבי יוחנן's view that the prohibition only starts at שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him from a source
An animal or bird with a deadly physical defect
A partner, here the new bird that replaces the unfit one
Permitted for benefit, meaning one may use it or profit from it
While still alive

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is challenging ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it was found to be a טריפה,
he takes a partner for the second one,
phrases.notes: The second one is the bird that is sent away alive. It needs a new partner to be slaughtered.

phrases.english: and the first one is permitted for benefit.
And if it enters your mind that it is forbidden while alive,
why is the first one permitted for benefit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 17 was answered, רבי יוחנן brings a new challenge against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the birds become forbidden while alive, as soon as they are taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prohibition that took effect while the bird was alive should stay in force even if the bird is later found to be a טריפה. Yet the משנה permits the bird.

steps.title: The defect was inside the bird from the start
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the משנה is talking about a bird whose defect was in its inner organs. Such a bird was never fit for the מצוה, so holiness never took hold of it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? A bird found to be a טריפה in its inner organs, so holiness never took effect on it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש narrows the case in the משנה so it fits his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש still holds that taking the bird forbids it while alive. Here, though, the bird was unfit from the very start, so the taking never worked and no prohibition began. That is why it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? Used to limit a source to a specific case
Its inner organs
Holiness, the special status that makes the bird forbidden

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, with what are we dealing?
Where it was found to be a טריפה in its inner organs,
so that holiness did not take effect on it at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that a bird taken for the מצוה is not forbidden while alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a bird that was never fit, so holiness never took effect. Normally, a fit bird would be forbidden from the taking.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a bird slaughtered without the other items
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא about a bird slaughtered without the hyssop, the cedar wood or the scarlet wool. רבי יעקב says it is forbidden because it was set aside for its מצוה. רבי שמעון says it is permitted because it was not slaughtered the proper way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If he slaughtered the bird without hyssop, without cedar wood, or without scarlet wool, רבי יעקב says: since it was set aside for its מצוה, it is forbidden. רבי שמעון says: since it was not slaughtered according to its מצוה, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a new source against ריש לקיש. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the next step will explain how it disproves ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions in the ברייתא focus on the שחיטה: was it done properly or not? רבי יוחנן will use this to show that the prohibition is linked to the שחיטה, not to the time the bird was alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, a plant used in the מצורע's purification
Cedar wood
Scarlet wool
It was set aside for its מצוה

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
If he slaughtered it without hyssop
or without cedar wood
or without scarlet wool,
רבי יעקב says:
Since it was set aside for its מצוה, it is forbidden.
רבי שמעון says:
Since it was slaughtered not according to its מצוה, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 answered the first challenge, רבי יוחנן brings a second source against ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: That the bird is not forbidden while alive, against ריש לקיש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a disagreement between רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the birds become forbidden while alive, as soon as they are taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both תנאים in the ברייתא decide the bird's status by the שחיטה. The next step spells out how this shows the bird was not forbidden while alive.

steps.title: Both opinions agree the bird is not forbidden while alive
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the ברייתא. רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון only disagree about whether an improper שחיטה counts as a שחיטה. Both agree that the bird does not become forbidden while it is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about this: one holds that an unfit שחיטה is still called a שחיטה, and the other holds that an unfit שחיטה is not called a שחיטה. But everyone agrees, at least, that the bird is not forbidden while it is alive!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן draws the conclusion from the ברייתא and uses it to attack ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bird were already forbidden while alive, as ריש לקיש says, it would not matter whether the שחיטה was proper. רבי שמעון could not permit it. Since both opinions make the outcome depend on the שחיטה, both seem to hold that the prohibition starts only at שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree about this point
A שחיטה that cannot fully achieve its purpose
It is still called a שחיטה, meaning it counts as one
According to everyone

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יעקב forbids the bird, but not because it was forbidden while alive. He forbids it because he holds that even an improper שחיטה counts, so the שחיטה itself makes it forbidden.

phrases.english: They disagree only
in this: one master holds:
phrases.notes: The first master is רבי יעקב, and the second master is רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: a slaughter that is not fit is called a slaughter,
and the other master holds:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה – לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: a slaughter that is not fit is not called a slaughter.
But according to everyone, at least,
it does not become forbidden while alive!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא מָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא quoted in step 21 into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the birds become forbidden while alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both תנאים make the prohibition depend on the שחיטה. That only makes sense if nothing became forbidden earlier, while the bird was alive.

steps.title: This is an argument among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that this question is an argument among תנאים, so he may follow a different תנא. He starts quoting a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל: one kind of מצוה that enables and one that atones is said about inside the מקדש, and the same pair is said about outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים. As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: a מצוה that enables and a מצוה that atones are stated about inside, and a מצוה that enables and a מצוה that atones are stated about outside.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש admits the ברייתא does not fit his view and says other תנאים agree with him. He begins quoting their teaching; the גמרא will finish explaining it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not reject the ברייתא. He says it reflects only one side of an argument among תנאים. The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל sets up a comparison between inside and outside, and that comparison will be used to support his view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument among תנאים
The school of רבי ישמעאל
Something that enables, making a person fit for a next step
Something that atones

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is speaking. He means some other תנא agrees with him, even if this ברייתא does not.

phrases.english: as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Something that enables and something that atones are stated inside,
phrases.notes: Inside means inside the מקדש. The גמרא will explain this comparison in the next lines.

phrases.english: and something that enables and something that atones are stated outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by showing that the issue is an argument among תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the question is an argument among תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone seemed to agree that the bird is not forbidden while alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: That agreement holds only for the תנאים of that ברייתא. The school of רבי ישמעאל has another view, and its derivation will support ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Enabling items are treated like atoning items, both inside and outside
steps.stepSummary: The teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל concludes. Inside the מקדש, the item that enables is treated like the item that atones. So outside the מקדש too, the enabling item (the מצורע's birds) is treated like the atoning item (the עגלה ערופה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as with the enabling and atoning items mentioned inside the מקדש, the תורה treated the enabling one like the atoning one, so too with the enabling and atoning items mentioned outside, the תורה treated the enabling one like the atoning one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the teaching that ריש לקיש began quoting in the last step. It shows that there is a תנא who agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה atones, and it is forbidden for benefit even before it is killed. This teaching says the מצורע's birds, which only enable him to become pure, follow the same rule. That means the birds can be forbidden while still alive, which is exactly ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that enables, making a person fit or ready (here, the מצורע's birds)
Something that atones (here, the עגלה ערופה)
Inside, meaning things done in the מקדש
Outside, meaning things done outside the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש is not alone. The school of רבי ישמעאל compares the מצורע's birds to the עגלה ערופה, so the birds can be forbidden even while alive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the answer to רבי יוחנן's question from the ברייתא. רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון may hold that the birds are not forbidden while alive, but ריש לקיש can follow this other תנא instead.

phrases.english: Just as with the enabling and atoning items mentioned for inside the מקדש,
the Torah made the enabling one like the atoning one,
so too with the enabling and atoning items mentioned for outside,
phrases.notes: Outside means the מצורע's birds (enabling) and the עגלה ערופה (atoning).

phrases.english: the Torah made the enabling one like the atoning one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote from the school of רבי ישמעאל that step 23 began
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the issue is an argument among תנאים, and ריש לקיש follows the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every תנא agrees that the birds are not forbidden while alive, so ריש לקיש has no support
steps.terutzMaskana: The school of רבי ישמעאל treats the enabling birds like the atoning עגלה ערופה, which is forbidden while alive

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: the sent-away bird is permitted and the slaughtered bird is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to an earlier ברייתא. The word 'all' in 'all pure birds you may eat' includes the bird that is sent away. The words 'these are what you shall not eat' include the bird that is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: 'All pure birds you may eat' comes to include the bird that is sent away. 'And these are what you shall not eat from them' comes to include the slaughtered bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to examine a ברייתא it quoted earlier, which learns about the מצורע's two birds from two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two neighboring פסוקים are split between the two birds. The permitting פסוק is applied to the living bird that is sent away. The forbidding פסוק is applied to the bird that is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself', going back to examine a source quoted earlier
The bird that is sent away alive
The bird that is slaughtered
To include

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two פסוקים. The permitting פסוק goes with the living, sent-away bird, and the forbidding פסוק goes with the slaughtered bird.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to look closely at the ברייתא it quoted earlier.

phrases.english: "All pure birds you may eat"
comes to include the bird that is sent away;
"And these are what you shall not eat from them"
comes to include the slaughtered bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש exchange to examine an earlier ברייתא on its own terms
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sent-away bird is permitted to eat, and the slaughtered bird is forbidden

steps.title: Why not flip the two פסוקים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we shouldn't reverse it, so that the slaughtered bird is permitted and the sent-away bird is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's choice of which bird gets which פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the wording of the פסוקים says which bird each one refers to. So the reading looks arbitrary unless there is a reason to prefer it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And I will reverse it', a challenge asking why not switch the two sides

phrases.english: But I can reverse it!
phrases.notes: He means: let the slaughtered bird be permitted and the sent-away bird be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way the ברייתא in step 25 assigned the פסוקים
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assignment of the permitting פסוק to the sent-away bird and the forbidding פסוק to the slaughtered bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים don't specify which bird is which, so the opposite reading seems just as possible

steps.title: A living kosher creature is never found to be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explains that we never find a living kosher creature that is forbidden. So the living, sent-away bird must be the permitted one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: We have not found living creatures that are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a reason why the ברייתא cannot be reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher creature that is alive and set free does not stay forbidden forever. So it makes sense that the forbidding פסוק goes with the slaughtered bird and the permitting פסוק goes with the living one.

keyTerms.meaning: Living creatures
We have not found, meaning there is no such case
The תנא whose teaching רבי יוחנן reports here

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי:
We have not found living creatures that are forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means kosher creatures that stay forbidden to eat for good.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a general principle that decides which reading is correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים could be applied to either bird
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a living kosher creature is never forbidden, the living bird is the permitted one

steps.title: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק begins to challenge the principle
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק objects to the claim that no living creature is ever forbidden. He starts to say, 'But aren't there...'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק objected to this: But aren't there...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבי יוחנן's principle. The rest of the objection continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק is about to bring examples of living kosher creatures that are forbidden. If he succeeds, the reason given for not reversing the ברייתא falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, introducing a challenge
But aren't there, the opening of a counterexample

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק objected to this:
But aren't there...

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle given in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's principle that no living kosher creature is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He is about to bring counterexamples of living creatures that are forbidden
